speakers: Jeffrey Hirsch (author, Stock Trader's Almanac; seasonality)
summary:
Eisman interviews Jeffrey Hirsch (Stock Trader's Almanac, April 2026) on calendar and seasonal patterns: midterm/four-year cycle, best six months, January barometer, intraday and monthly flows, sector seasonals, Bitcoin, super boom.
Patterns persist because humans (and the people who program algorithms) behave habitually and institutions rebalance on calendar dates.
Main views: midterm-year bottom Q2-Q3 then strong Q4-Q2 rally; AI as the super-boom technology; credit cycle tightening.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: we are creatures of habit. We do things uh repeatedly um habitually with our money
claims.claim: Calendar patterns arise because people and institutions behave repetitively (daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, four-year, presidential cycle), so market behavior has regular seasonal structure.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: in the last 19 cycles, it's like 11 of the last 16 bare markets bottomed in the midterm year
claims.claim: 11 of the last 16 bear markets bottomed in a US midterm year, the 'bottom picker's paradise'.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: the weakest period what we call the weak spot of the four-year cycle is Q2 Q3 of the midterm year
claims.claim: Q2-Q3 of the midterm year is the weak spot of the four-year cycle because campaigning draws attention from the market and economy, leaving it choppy and vulnerable.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: The gain from the midterm low to the pre-election year high is 46.3% for the Dow on average going back to 1914
claims.claim: From midterm-year low to pre-election-year high the Dow gains 46.3% on average since 1914 (Nasdaq 66.6%); the pre-election year is the best year of the cycle.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: the sweet spot of the four-year cycle is Q4 midterm year to Q2 pre-election year
claims.claim: Sweet spot is Q4 of the midterm year to Q2 of the pre-election year, averaging about 19% Dow, 20% S&P, 29% Nasdaq.
claims.direction: long equities Q4 midterm through Q2 pre-election

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: The most important one is the best six months
claims.claim: Best six months switching strategy (invested Nov-Apr, defensive May-Oct), introduced in 1986/87, is the most important seasonal pattern.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: Instead of sell May and go, you can't sell in May and go away if you didn't buy in October
claims.claim: 'Sell in May' needs a 'buy in October' companion; the Almanac does not go fully away in summer but tightens up, limits new longs, sells losers and repositions defensively (Nasdaq best eight months).

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: use the MACD to sort of confirm an entry or exit
claims.claim: MACD momentum is used with seasonality as a confirmation signal for entry and exit of the best-six-months switch, not alone.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: go against your instincts. You know, sell your losers short or fast and hang let your winners ride
claims.claim: Loeb rules: cut losers fast, let winners ride; they also sell half on a double and take profits.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: 6,200 and change different blackbox systems
claims.claim: Aronson tested 6,200+ black-box systems against a null hypothesis of no predictive power and all failed; the best-six-months strategy tested out of sample since 1987 passed.
claims.testable: yes - this is a testing method

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: there is that mutual fund deadline um the 40 act uh deadline of October 31st
claims.claim: The October 31 fiscal year end for mutual funds (40 Act) forces institutional trades, one reason for the autumn low and seasonal start.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: institution has a stock that's down 50%. It's an embarrassment
claims.claim: Window dressing: institutions sell losers before quarter-end reports so investors do not see them, pressing September weakness and October lows.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: money following money, gains be get gains
claims.claim: Year-end performance chasing by institutions plus retail holiday money and bonuses push November-January, the best three months.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: the monthly five-day bulge
claims.claim: The old pattern of gains in the last and first days of the month has weakened; a mid-month spike now appears from bi-weekly payroll deductions into 401(k) funds, which must be invested.
claims.direction: long around mid-month and turn of month
claims.conditions: patterns shift and are re-checked every year

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: mutual funds are only allowed to have a certain amount of cash
claims.claim: Mutual funds limited in cash holdings must buy as 401(k) inflows arrive, creating predictable demand ('super eight days').

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: the beginning of of of August is notoriously weak
claims.claim: Each month has a personality: early August is weak and turn-of-month in October-November is strong.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: the opens are weak which is sort of the dumb money you know in the morning
claims.claim: Intraday Dow pattern: weak opens, low around 10-10:30, lunch lull, drag at 2-2:30, then an end-of-day rally from smart money; persists despite algorithms because people program them.
claims.direction: buy limit near 2:30; weak open, strong close

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: normally um and I'm in the XLU uh um recently with our seasonal trade
claims.claim: Utilities seasonal trade March-October (worst six months defensive); pattern strengthened by data center electricity demand.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: copper tends to make its low in December when the construction you know activity is at its seasonal low
claims.claim: Copper and energy (XLE) tend to bottom in December and peak April-May, with construction activity seasonality.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: Seasonality, fundamentals, technicals, monetary policy, and sentiment
claims.claim: Almanac uses five disciplines together: seasonality, fundamentals, technicals, monetary policy and sentiment.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: the indicator graveyard
claims.claim: Patterns decay: the September reverse barometer and small-cap January effect no longer work (small-cap outperformance now starts late December).

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: as January goes, so goes the year
claims.claim: January barometer: S&P 500 direction in January (and first five days) predicts the year's direction.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: When all three are up, you get the market up 90.6% of the time
claims.claim: January trifecta (Santa Claus rally, first five days, full-month barometer): all three up leads to higher market 90.6% of the time (29 of 32); two of three leaves S&P up next 11 months 87.5% of the time (+12.2%).
claims.indicator: Santa Claus rally, first five days, January barometer

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: the lame duck amendment to the constitution
claims.claim: January barometer exists because Congress, inauguration and White House priorities begin in January, so markets reflect the forecast for the year.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: it hasn't performed seasonally. It's very weak in midterm election years
claims.claim: Bitcoin seasonality (low late September) failed last year; weak in midterm years.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: If the market doesn't rally, you know, during the bullish seasonal period
claims.claim: Gul's rule: if a market fails to rally in its bullish seasonal period, other forces are stronger and will assert themselves when the period ends.

claims.speaker: Eisman
claims.quote: My my problem with Bitcoin is it acts
claims.claim: Bitcoin acts opposite to its thesis (a levered Nasdaq with unclear closing price and no recourse on theft).

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: the market makes these 500 500% moves following war and inflation
claims.claim: Super boom thesis: after war and inflation the market makes ~500% moves, enabled by a paradigm-shifting technology (car, interstate, microprocessor, now AI).

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: the market sort of bottom within a month or so of the of the initial outset on average
claims.claim: Markets bottom within about a month of a war's outset on average; shorter wars mean faster recoveries, and oil rises like a rocket and falls like a feather.

claims.speaker: Jeffrey
claims.quote: the taco trade seasonal cycle
claims.claim: Trump-years pattern: Q1 shocks, double bottom late March/early April, then rally averaging about 15% through year end.

claims.speaker: Eisman
claims.quote: almost 100% of all the loan growth in the United States since the great financial crisis has been in private credit
claims.claim: Almost all post-GFC US loan growth was in private credit, so a credit cycle tightening could slow the economy though banks are not at risk.

claims.speaker: Eisman
claims.quote: who creates the algorithms? People
claims.claim: Stock trading has patterns because people buy stocks and humans program algorithms.
